questions.q: Let $x = 2$~be a local minima of the function $f  \left(x\right) = 2x^{4} - 18x^{2} + 8x + 12, x \in \left(-4, 4\right)$. If $M$ is local maximum value of the function $f$ in  \left(-4, 4\right)$, then $M =
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,&

$x = 2$~be a local minima of the function $f \left(x\right) = 2x^{4} - 18x^{2} + 8x + 12, x \in \left(-4, 4\right)$

Now differentiating the above function we get,

$f^{'} \left(x\right) = 8x^{3} - 36x + 8$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = 4\left(2x^{3} - 9x + 2\right)$

Now equating it to zero we get,~$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2x^{3} - 9x + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 2\right)\left(2x^{2} + 4x - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{- 4 \pm \sqrt{24}}{4}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{- 2 \pm \sqrt{6}}{2}$

$∴ x = \dfrac{\sqrt{6} - 2}{2}$~{by checking sign change of $f^{'} \left($x\right)$~for maxima}

Now rewriting~f\left($x\right) = 2x^{4} - 18x^{2} + 8x + 12$~we get,

f\left($x\right) = \left($x^{2} - 2x - \dfrac{9}{2}\right)\left(2x^{2} + 4x - 1\right) + 24x + 7 . 5$

Hence,~f\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{6} - 2}{2}\right) =$M = 12\sqrt{6} - \dfrac{33}{2}

$

questions.q: The curve $y  \left(x\right) = ax^{3} + bx^{2} + cx + 5$ touches the $x$-axis at the point $P\left(-2, 0\right)$ and cuts the $y$-axis at the point $\mathrm{Q}$, where $y^{'}$ is equal to $3$. Then the local maximum value of $y  \left(x\right)$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given that& $y \left(x\right) = ax^{3} + bx^{2} + cx + 5$ pass~through \left(-2, 0\right)$~

so~$8a - 4b + 2c = 5 . . . \left(i\right)$

Since the curve touches~$x$-axis at~ \left(-2, 0\right)$, so its slope would be~$0$

i.e~$y^{'}\left(-2\right) = 0 ⇒ \left($3ax^{2} + 2bx + c\right)x = - 2 = 0$

$12a - 4b + c = 0 . . . \left($ii\right)$

Also given, for~$x = 0, y^{'}( x ) = 3$

$c = 3 . . . \left($iii\right)$

Solving eq.~ \left(i\right), \left(ii\right) \text{ and } \left(iii\right)$, we get,~

$a = - $\dfrac{1}{2},$b = - $\dfrac{3}{4}

For local maxima~$y^{'} \left($x\right) = - \dfrac{3}{2}x^{2} - \dfrac{3}{2}x + 3 = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + x - 2 = 0 ⇒ \left($x - 1\right) \left(x + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 1$~and~$y^{"}\left(1\right) < 0$

So~$y\left(x\right)$ has local maxima at~$x = 1$

Hence,~$y\left(1\right) = \dfrac{27}{4}$

$

questions.q: The number of distinct real roots of the equation $x^{7} - 7x - 2 = 0$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$x^{7} - 7x - 2 = 0$

$x^{7} - 7x = 2$

Now taking $f\left(x\right) = x^{7} - 7x$ (odd) & $y = 2$

Now differentiating $f\left(x\right)$ w.r.t $x$ we get,

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 7\left(x^{6} - 1\right) = 7\left(x^{2} - 1\right)\left(x^{4} + x^{2} + 1\right)$

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 0 ⇒ x = \pm 1$

So points of extrema are $- 1 \text{ and } 1$, Now plotting the graph to check number of solution we get,

$f\left(x\right) = 2$ has $3$ real distinct solution.

questions.q: The height of a right circular cylinder of maximum volume inscribed in a sphere of radius $3$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
From the diagram, we get radius of cylinder $= \sqrt{R^{2} - {\left(\dfrac{h}{2}\right)}^{2}}$
$⇒$ Volume of cylinder $V = \pi\left(R^{2} - \dfrac{h^{2}}{4}\right)h$
For maximum volume: $\dfrac{dV}{dh} = 0$
$⇒ \pi\left(R^{2} - \dfrac{{3h}^{2}}{4}\right) = 0$
$⇒ h^{2} = \dfrac{4R^{2}}{3} = \dfrac{4 \times 9}{3} = 12$
$⇒ h = 2\sqrt{3}$

questions.q: Let $g ( x ) = 3f\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + f ( 3 - x )$ and $f^{"} ( x ) > 0$ for all $x \in ( 0, 3 )$. If $g$ is decreasing in $( 0, \alpha )$ and increasing in $( \alpha, 3 )$, then $8\alpha$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $g ( x ) = 3f\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + f ( 3 - x )$ and $f^{"} ( x ) > 0 \forall x \in ( 0, 3 )$

$⇒ f^{'} ( x )$ is increasing function

$⇒ g^{'} ( x ) = 3 \times \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot f^{'}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) - f^{'} ( 3 - x )$

$⇒ g^{'} ( x ) = f^{'} \left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) -$f^{'} ( 3 - x )$

It is given that $g$ is decreasing in \left($0, $\alpha\right)$ then g^{'} ( x ) < 0$.

$⇒ f^{'} \left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) -$f^{'} ( 3 - x ) < 0$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$< f^{'} ( 3 - x )$

$⇒ $\dfrac{x}{3}$< 3 - x$

$⇒ x < 9 - 3x$

$⇒ x < $\dfrac{9}{4}

$⇒ $\alpha = \dfrac{9}{4}

$⇒ 8$\alpha =$8 $\times \dfrac{9}{4}

$⇒ 8$\alpha =$18$

$

questions.q: Let $f: \left(- 1, \infty\right) \to R$~be defined by $f\left(0\right) = 1$~and $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{x}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(1 + x\right), x \ne 0$. Then the function $f$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{x}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(1 + x\right), x \ne 0$

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{\dfrac{x}{1 + x} - \ln \left(1 + x\right)}{x2} = \dfrac{x - \left(1 + x\right)\ln \left(1 + x\right)}{x^{2} \left(1 + x\right)}$

Let~$g\left(x\right) = x - \left(1 + x\right)\ln \left($1 + x\right)$

$g^{'} \left($x\right) = - \ln \left($1 + x\right)$

$⇒ g^{'}\left($x\right)\left\{$\begin{cases}> 0 & \forall x \in \left(-1, 0\right) \\ < 0 & \forall x \in \left(0, \infty\right)\end{cases}$\right

${g}_\max$ at $x = 0 ⇒ g \left($0\right) = 0$~is the maximum value

So,~g\left($x\right) < 0 \forall x \in \left(-$1, $\infty\right)$⇒ f^{'} \left(x\right) < 0 \forall x \in \left(-$1, $\infty\right)

Hence,~$f \left($x\right)$~is~decreasing~$\forall x \in \left(-$1, $\infty\right)

$

questions.q: The sum of the absolute minimum and the absolute maximum values of the function $f \left(x\right) =  \left|$3x - x^{2} + 2\right| - x$~in the interval~\left[-$1, 2\right]$& is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $f\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}x^{2} - 4x - 2, & \forall x \in \left(- 1, \dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2}\right) \\ - x^{2} + 2x + 2, & \forall x \in [ \dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2}, 2 )\end{cases}$\right

When~$x \in \left(-$1, $\dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2}\right)

$f^{'}\left($x\right) = 2x - 4 = 0 ⇒ x = 2$

Now~$f\left($2\right) = 2$,~$f\left(-$1\right) = 3$

$f\left(\dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{17} - 3}{2}

When~$x \in [ $\dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2},$2 )$

$f^{'} \left(x\right) = - 2x + 2$

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = - 2\left(x - 1\right)$

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$~when~$x = 1$

$f\left(1\right) = 3$

Hece, absolute minimum value~$= \dfrac{\sqrt{17} - 3}{2}$

and absolute maximum value~$= 3$

Sum~$= \dfrac{\sqrt{17} - 3}{2} + 3 = \dfrac{\sqrt{17} + 3}{2}$

$

questions.q: Let the function $f(x)=\frac{x}{3}+\frac{3}{x}+3, x \neq 0$ be strictly increasing in  \left(-\infty, \alpha_1\right) \mathrm{U}\left(\alpha_2, \infty\right)$ and strictly decreasing in  \left(\alpha_3, \alpha_4\right) \mathrm{U}\left(\alpha_4, \alpha_5\right)$. Then $\sum_{\mathrm{i}=1}^5 \alpha_{\mathrm{i}}^2$ is equal to :-
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & f(x)=\frac{x}{3}+\frac{3}{x}+3, x \neq 0 \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{1}{3}-\frac{3}{x^2}=0 \quad \Rightarrow x= \pm 3 \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{x^2-3}{3 x^2}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrmf^{\prime}(\mathrm{x}) \gt 0 \forall(-\infty,-3) \cup(3, \infty) \rightarrow \text { increasing } \\ & \mathrmf^{\prime}(\mathrm{x}) \lt 0 \forall(-3,0) \cup(0,3) \rightarrow \text { decreasing }\end{aligned}$
$\sum_{i=1}^5 \alpha_i^2=(-3)^2+(3)^2+(-3)^2+(0)^2+(3)^2$
$=36$

questions.q: If $m$ is the minimum value of $k$ for which the function $f\left(x\right) = x\sqrt{kx - x^{2}}$ is increasing in the interval $[ 0,3 ]$ and $M$ is the maximum value of $f$ in $[ 0,3 ]$ when $k = m,$ then the ordered pair $( m, M )$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = x\sqrt{kx - x^{2}}{⇒ f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{3kx - 4x^{2}}{2\sqrt{kx - x^{2}}}$
As per the given condition $f^{'} \left(x\right) ≥ 0$ for $x \in \left[0,3\right]$
$⇒ 3kx - 4x^{2} ≥ 0$ for $x \in \left[0,3\right]$
$⇒ 3k - 4x ≥ 0$ for $x \in \left[0,3\right]$
$⇒ k \ge $\dfrac{4x}{3}for $x \in \left[$0,3\right]$
$⇒ k ≥ 4$ . So minimum value of $k$ is $m = 4 .$
Now f\left($x\right) = $x\sqrt{4x - x^{2}}
Since given function in increasing hence maximum value will occur at $x = 3$
$⇒ f ( 3 ) = $3\sqrt{4 \times 3 - {3}^{2}} =3\sqrt{3},$M = $3\sqrt{3}
Hence $( m, M ) = ( 4, $3\sqrt{3} )$

questions.q: A wire of length $20m$ is to be cut into two pieces. A piece of length ${ℓ}_{1}$~is bent to make a square of area ${A}_{1}$~and the other piece of length ${ℓ}_{2}$~is made into a circle of area ${A}_{2}$. If $2{A}_{1} + 3{A}_{2}$~is minimum then \left(\pi{ℓ}_{1}\right): {ℓ}_{2}$ \text{ and } is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The length of wire is& $20m$.

According to the question:

${ℓ}_{1} + {ℓ}_{2} = 20$

$⇒ \dfrac{d{ℓ}_{2}}{d{ℓ}_{1}} = - 1$

Let the side of the square be~$x$, then

$4x = {ℓ}_{1}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{ℓ1}{4} . . . \left(1\right)$

Let the radius~of the circle be~$y$, then

~$2\piy = {ℓ}_{2}$

$⇒ y = $\dfrac{ℓ2}{2\pi} . . . \left(2\right)$

Hence,

${A}_{1} = \left(\dfrac{ℓ1}{4})$2$~and~${A}_{2} = \pi\left(\dfrac{ℓ2}{2\pi})$2$

Let~$S = 2{A}_{1} + 3{A}_{2}$

$⇒ S = $\dfrac{( {ℓ}_{1}{)}^{2}}{8} + \dfrac{3 ( {ℓ}_{2}{)}^{2}}{4\pi}

$⇒ $\dfrac{dS}{d{ℓ}_{1}} = \dfrac{2{ℓ}_{1}}{8} + \dfrac{6{ℓ}_{2}}{4\pi} \cdot \left(\dfrac{d{ℓ}_{2}}{d{ℓ}_{1}}\right)$

For~$S$~to be minimum,

$\dfrac{ds}{d{ℓ}_{1}} =0$

$⇒ \dfrac{2{ℓ}_{1}}{8} + \dfrac{6{ℓ}_{2}}{4\pi} \cdot \left(\dfrac{d{ℓ}_{2}}{d{ℓ}_{1}}\right) =0$

$⇒ \dfrac{2{ℓ}_{1}}{8} - \dfrac{6{ℓ}_{2}}{4\pi} =0 \left(∵ $\dfrac{d{ℓ}_{2}}{d{ℓ}_{1}} = -$1\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{ℓ1}{4} = \dfrac{6{ℓ}_{2}}{4\pi}

$⇒ $\dfrac{\pi{ℓ}_{1}}{ℓ2} =$6$

questions.q: If the function $f$ given by $f\left(x\right) = x^{3} - 3  \left(a - 2\right)x^{2} + 3ax + 7$, for some $a \in R$ is increasing in \left(0, 1\right]$ and decreasing in  \left[1, 5\right)$, then a root of the equation, \dfrac{f  \left(x\right) - 14}{ \left($x - 1\right)2}$ =0, \left($x \ne 1\right) is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
At $x = 1, f^{′}\left(x\right) = 0$

$∴ f^{′}\left(x\right) = 3x^{2} - 6\left(a - 2\right)x + 3a$

Now,~$f^{'}\left(1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3 - 6\left(a - 2\right) + 3a = 0$

$⇒ a = 5$

$∴ \dfrac{f\left(x\right) - 14}{\left(x - 1\right)2} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{x^{3} - 9x^{2} + 15x - 7}{\left(x - 1\right)2} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(x - 7\right)\left(x^{2} - 2x + 1\right)}{\left(x - 1\right)2} = 0$

$⇒ x - 7 = 0 ⇒ x = 7$

$\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{f(x)}{x^2}=5 \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\left.a x^4+b x^3+c x^2+d x+e\right)}{x^2}=5 \\ & c=5 \text { and } d=e=0 \\ & f(x)=a x^4+b x^3+5 x^2 \\ & f^{\prime}(x)=4 a x^3+3 b x^2+10 x \\ & =x\left(4 a x^2+3 b x+10\right)
\end{aligned}$
has extremes at 4 and so $f^{\prime}(4)=0 \ \text{ and } f^{\prime}(5)=0$
so $\mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{8} \ \text{ and } \mathrm{~b}=\frac{-3}{2}$
$\text { so } f(2)=\frac{1}{8} \times 2^4-\frac{3}{2} \times 2^3+5 \times 2^2$
$=2-12+20=10 $

questions.q: If the maximum value of $a$, for which the function ${f}_{a}\left(x\right) = \tan^{- 1}2x - 3ax + 7$~is non-decreasing in  \left(- \dfrac{π}{6}, \dfrac{π}{6}\right)$, is $\overset{¯}{a}$, then $f\overset{¯}{a}  \left(\dfrac{π}{8}\right)$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& ${f}_{a}\left(x\right) = \tan^{- 1}2x - 3ax + 7$~is non-decreasing function in \left(- \dfrac{π}{6}, \dfrac{π}{6}\right)$, so~

${fa}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2}{1 + 4x^{2}} - 3a \ge 0$

i.e.~$a \le \left(\dfrac{2}{3\left(1 + 4x^{2}\right)}\right)min$~

Now, maximum value of $a$~is at~$x = 0$

i.e.~${a}_\max = \overset{¯}{a} = \dfrac{6}{9 + {π}^{2}}$

Hence,~$f\overset{¯}{a}\left(\dfrac{π}{8}\right) = \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{π}{4} - 3\left(\dfrac{6}{9 + {π}^{2}}\right)\left(\dfrac{π}{8}\right) + 7$

$= \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{π}{4} - \dfrac{9\pi}{4\left({π}^{2} + 9\right)} + 7 = 8 - \dfrac{9\pi}{4\left({π}^{2} + 9\right)}$

$

questions.q: Let $a$~be an integer such that all the real roots of the polynomial~$2x^{5} + 5x^{4} + 10x^{3} + 10x^{2} + 10x + 10$ lie in the interval  \left(a, a + 1\right)$. Then, $| a |$ is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $2x^{5} + 5x^{4} + 10x^{3} + 10x^{2} + 10x + 10 = f \left(x\right)$

Now $f \left(-2\right) = - 34$ and $f\left(-1\right) = 3$

Hence $f\left(x\right)$ has a root in \left(-2, - 1\right)$

Further $f^{'}\left(x\right) = 10x^{4} + 20x^{3} + 30x^{2} + 20x + 10$

$= 10x^{2} \left($x^{2} + 2x + 3 + $\dfrac{2}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)

$= 10x^{2} \left[ \left(x^{2} + $\dfrac{1}{x2}\right) +$2\left(x + $\dfrac{1}{x}\right) +$3\right]$

$= 10x^{2} \left[ \left($x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)2 - 2 + $2 \left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right) +3\right]$

$= 10x^{2} \left[ \left($x + $\dfrac{1}{x} +$1\right)2\right] > 0$ for all $x$~belongs to~$R$.

$f\left($x\right)$~is strictly increasing function. Since it is an odd degree polynomial it will have exactly one real root.

Hence, $f \left(x\right)$ has only one real root, so \left|a\right| = 2$.

$

questions.q: Let the set of all positive values of $\lambda$, for which the point of local minimum of the function  \left(1+x \left(\lambda^2-$x^2\right)\right)$ satisfies \frac{x^2+x+2}{x^2+5 x+6} \lt$0$, be $(\alpha, \beta).$Then $\aalpha^2+\beta^2 is equal to _________$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{x^2+x+2}{x^2+5 x+6} \lt 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{(x+2)(x+3)} \lt 0\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & x \in(-3,-2) \ldots \ldots \ldots . .(1) \\ & f(x)=1+x\left(\lambda^2-x^2\right) \end{aligned}$
Finding local minima $f^{\prime}(x)=\left(\lambda^2-x^2\right)+(-2 x) \cdot x$ Put $\mathrmf^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=0$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \lambda^2=3 x^2 \\ & \Rightarrow x= \pm \frac{\lambda}{\sqrt{3}} \end{aligned}$$ We want local min $\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{-\lambda}{\sqrt{3}}$ from (1) $x \in(-3,-2)$\begin{aligned} & -3 \lt \frac{-\lambda}{\sqrt{3}} \lt -2 \\ & 3 \sqrt{3} \gt \lambda \gt 2 \sqrt{3} \\ & \alpha=2 \sqrt{3}, \beta=3 \sqrt{3} \\ & \alpha^2+\beta^2=12+27=39\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = \left|\left(x - 1\right)\left(x^{2} - 2x - 3\right)\right| + x - 3, x \in \mathbb{R}$. If~$m$ and $M$~are respectively the number of points of local minimum and local maximum of $f$ in the interval  \left(0, 4\right)$, then $m + M$& is equal to _____.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f \left(x\right) = \left| \left(x - 1\right)\left($x + 1\right)\left(x - 3\right)\right| + \left(x - 3\right)$

$f\left(x\right) = \left\${$\begin{cases} \left(x - 3\right)\left(x^{2}\right), \text{ and } 3 ≤ x ≤ 4 \\ \left(x - 3\right)\left(2 - x^{2}\right), \text{ and } 1 ≤ x < 3 \\ \left(x - 3\right)\left(x^{2}\right), \text{ and } 0 < x < 1\end{cases}$\right

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}3x^{2} - 6x, & 3 < x < 4 \\ - 3x^{2} + 6x + 2, & 1 < x < 3 \\ 3x^{2} - 6x, & 0 < x < 1\end{cases}$\right

$f^{'}\left({3}^{+}\right) > 0f^{'}\left({3}^{-}\right) < 0 \to$ Minimum

$f^{'}\left({1}^{+}\right) > 0f^{'}\left({1}^{-}\right) < 0 \to$ Minimum

For $x \in \left(1, 3\right), f^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$~at one point → Maximum

For $x \in \left(3, 4\right), f^{'}\left(x\right) \ne 0$

For $x \in \left(0, 1\right), f^{'}\left(x\right) + 0$

So points of minima are~$2$, so~$m = 2$

and point~of maxima is~$1$, so~$M = 1$

So,~$M + n = 3$

questions.q: The minimum value of $\alpha$ for which the equation $\dfrac{4}{\sin x} + \dfrac{1}{1 - \sin x} = \alpha$ has at least one solution in  \left(0, \dfrac{π}{2}\right)$ is______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{4}{\sin x} + \dfrac{1}{1 - \sin x}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{4}{\sin x} + \dfrac{1 + \sin x}{1 - \sin^{2}x}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = 4cosecx + \sec^{2}x + \tan x \sec x$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 4\cos x}{\sin^{2}x} + \dfrac{2\sin x + 1}{\cos^{3}x} + \dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{\cos^{3}x}$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 4\cos x}{\sin^{2}x} + \dfrac{\left(\sin x + 1\right)2}{\cos^{3}x}$

$⇒ f^{' '}\left(x\right) = - 4\left[\dfrac{- \sin^{3}x - 2\sin x\cos^{2}x}{\sin^{4}x}\right] + \dfrac{2\left(\sin x + 1\right)\cos^{4}x + 3\cos^{2}xsinx\left(\sin x + 1\right)2}{\cos^{6}x}$

$⇒ f^{' '}\left(x\right) = - 4\left[\dfrac{- \sin^{3}x - 2\sin x\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)}{\sin^{4}x}\right] + \dfrac{2\left(\sin x + 1\right)\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)2 + 3\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)\sin x\left(\sin x + 1\right)2}{\left(1 - \sin^{2}x\right)3}$

For critical points,

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(\sin x + 1\right)2}{\cos^{3}x} = \dfrac{4\cos x}{\sin^{2}x}$

$⇒ \sin^{2}x\left(\sin x + 1\right)2 = 4\cos^{4}x$

$⇒ \sin x\left(\sin x + 1\right) = 2\cos^{2}x$

$⇒ \sin^{2}x + \sin x = 2 - 2\sin^{2}x$

$⇒ 3\sin^{2}x + \sin x - 2 = 0$

$⇒ 3\sin^{2}x + 3\sin x - 2\sin x - 2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(3\sin x - 2\right)\left(\sin x + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \sin x = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Since,~$\sin x > 0 \forall x \in \left($0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right)

Now, at~$\sin x = $\dfrac{2}{3}, we get

$⇒ f^{' '}\left($x\right) = - 4\left[\dfrac{- \dfrac{8}{27} - \dfrac{4}{3}\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right)}{\dfrac{16}{81}}\right] + \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{5}{3}\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right)2 + 3\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right) \times \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{25}{9}}{\left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right)3}

$⇒ f^{' '}\left($x\right) = \left[$4\left[\dfrac{28}{27} \times \dfrac{81}{16}\right] + \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{5}{3}\left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right)2 + 3 \left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right) \times \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dddfrac{25}{9}}{ \left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right)3}\right]$> 0$

Hence, it is the point of minima.

$∴ $f\left($x\right)min = $\dfrac{4}{\dfrac{2}{3}} + \dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{2}{3}} =$9$

$f \left(x\right)max \to \infty$

$f\left(x\right)$ is continuous function

$∴ {α}_\min = 9$

questions.q: Let $f  \left(x\right)$~be a polynomial of degree $6$ in $x,$~in which the coefficient of $x^{6}$ is unity and it has extrema at $x = - 1$~and $x = 1$. If $\lim_{x \to 0}$\dfrac{f  \left(x\right)}{x3} =$1,$ then $5 \cdotf\left(2\right)$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $f\left(x\right) = x^{6} + ax^{5} + bx^{4} + cx^{3} + dx^{2} + ex + f$

as~$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x3} = 1$~non-zero finite

So,~$d = e = f = 0$

and~$f \left(x\right) = x^{3} \left($x^{3} + ax^{2} + bx + c\right)$

Hence,~$\lim_{x \to $0}\d$dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x3} =$c = 1$

Now, as~f\left($x\right) = x^{6} + ax^{5} + bx^{4} + x^{3}$

and~$f^{'}\left($x\right) = 0$~at~$x = 1$~and~$x = - 1$

i.e.,~$f^{'}\left($x\right) = 6x^{5} + 5ax^{4} + 4bx^{3} + 3x^{2}$

$f ' \left($1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 6 + 5a + 4b + 3 = 0$

$⇒ 5a + 4b = - 9$

and~$f^{'}\left(-$1\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 6 + 5a - 4b + 3 = 0$

$⇒ 5a - 4b = 3$

Solving both we get,

$a = \dfrac{- 6}{10} = \dfrac{- 3}{5}; b = \dfrac{- 3}{2}$

$∴ $f\left($x\right) = x^{6} - \dfrac{3}{5}x^{5} - \dfrac{3}{2}x^{4} + x^{3}$

$∴ 5f \left($2\right) = 5 \left[$64 - \dfrac{3}{5} \cdot32 - \dfrac{3}{2} \cdot16 + 8\right]$

$= 320 - 96 - 120 + 40$

$= 144$
